items.title: 当 AI 开始写 80% 的代码，架构才是真正的护城河
items.raw_excerpt: GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke 近日发出了一则措辞严厉的警告：“要么拥抱 AI，要么离开这个职业。”但所谓拥抱 AI，并不只是使用代码自动补全工具那么简单。它意味着我们核心能力的一次转移——从对语法的熟练掌握，转向系统思维（Systems Thinking），学会把问题不断拆解，直到小到可以交由 AI 去解决。一句话概括：我们现在都是架构师了。

title_i18n.zh: 当 AI 开始写 80% 的代码，架构才是真正的护城河
title_i18n.en: When AI writes 80% of the code, architecture becomes the true moat.
title_i18n.es: Cuando la IA comienza a escribir el 80% del código, la arquitectura se convierte en la verdadera barrera defensiva.

excerpt_i18n.zh: GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke 近日发出了一则措辞严厉的警告：“要么拥抱 AI，要么离开这个职业。”但所谓拥抱 AI，并不只是使用代码自动补全工具那么简单。它意味着我们核心能力的一次转移——从对语法的熟练掌握，转向系统思维（Systems Thinking），学会把问题不断拆解，直到小到可以交由 AI 去解决。一句话概括：我们现在都是架构师了。
excerpt_i18n.en: GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke recently issued a stern warning: "Embrace AI or leave the profession." However, embracing AI is not just about using code autocompletion tools. It signifies a shift in our core competencies—from mastering syntax to systems thinking, learning to break down problems until they are small enough for AI to solve. In short, we are all architects now.
excerpt_i18n.es: El CEO de GitHub, Thomas Dohmke, ha emitido recientemente una severa advertencia: "Adopta la IA o abandona la profesión". Pero adoptar la IA no se trata simplemente de usar herramientas de autocompletado de código. Significa un cambio en nuestras capacidades fundamentales: pasar del dominio de la sintaxis al pensamiento sistémico, aprendiendo a descomponer problemas hasta que sean lo suficientemente pequeños para que la IA los resuelva. En resumen: ahora todos somos arquitectos.

excerpt_i18n.en: On February 5, Li Xiang, Chairman of Li Auto, stated on social media that the new Li L9 will be the pioneering work of embodied intelligent robots. excerpt_i18n.en:
In cardiovascular disease prevention, a long-standing challenge is that many conditions remain latent in the body for years before onset, making it difficult to accurately predict early on whether an individual will face multiple cardiovascular disease risks simultaneously. Traditional risk assessments have primarily relied on conventional clinical indicators such as age, blood pressure, and lipid levels, or polygenic risk scores. However, cardiovascular diseases often involve a long-term evolution with multiple potential outcomes, making it hard for single indicators or disease-specific prediction methods to fully capture the true risk.

With advances in large-scale population cohorts and high-throughput molecular detection technologies, researchers have found that proteins and metabolites in the blood can more directly reflect the body’s current physiological state and disease progression. These molecular signals are influenced not only by genetic factors but also by environmental and lifestyle changes, providing new sources of information for long-term risk assessment.

Against this backdrop, a research team led by Associate Professor Zhang Qingpeng from the University of Hong Kong’s Data Science Institute and Department of Pharmacology and Pharmacy conducted a study integrating multiomics information with artificial intelligence, based on large-scale prospective population data from the UK Biobank. Moving beyond the "one disease, one model" approach, the team incorporated proteomic and metabolomic information into a unified framework to simultaneously assess long-term risks for multiple cardiovascular diseases. Las evaluaciones de riesgo tradicionales se basan principalmente en indicadores clínicos convencionales como edad, presión arterial y niveles de lípidos, o en puntuaciones de riesgo genético poligénico. Sin embargo, las enfermedades cardiovasculares suelen evolucionar a largo plazo y pueden presentar múltiples desenlaces simultáneos, por lo que un único indicador o un enfoque predictivo centrado en una sola enfermedad difícilmente refleja el riesgo real de manera integral.
